spec: Polity layer, planned by towns only (no player verbs yet). techs: a town researches the cheapest available tech once it holds the buildings (needs.buildings = count of finished claims by kind) and prerequisite techs; knowledge accrues from workshops and gifted villagers, and each tech already known makes the next dearer (tuning.costRisePerTech). Techs sharing a fork are rival paths: a town that takes one can never take (or be taught) the other. Deep shafts follow the masonry path, so a long-saws town never digs them. A town that loses a war forgets its newest tech and its banked knowledge. Feud roots: border tension, clashing creeds (friction above decay, so they never settle alone), rival doctrines, requests a linked neighbour could have filled but did not, and carts lost on a shared road; despair sharpens them all. spareDays/spareFlat/foodPool mirror logistics' surplus rule. mul = production multiplier per trade. creeds: a town that finishes a chapel founds one, chosen from the seed. tuning: every knob of tickPolity (feud sources, treaty and war thresholds, knowledge). See PLAN.md, Economy sim phase 8.

tuning.balanceNote: breakFeud 40 -> 20, warFeud 80 -> 20, truceFeud 35 -> 12 (game/scripts/balance-probe.mts). Feuds peak around 14-26 in a 120-day run, so 80 meant no war ever began. At 20 a treaty breaks where a new one could not form (tradeFeud), a war can follow, and a truce leaves the feud below the war line. Wars come out rare but present: about 0.1-0.4 per 120-day run, in every probed seed.
